en.headline: Man loses over HK$2.8 million in recyclable-waste investment scam
en.dek: Police recorded more than 50 investment fraud cases in the past week with total losses exceeding HK$30 million; fraudsters posed as electricity company staff.
body: A man in his 60s lost more than HK$2.8 million after being lured into a fake “recyclable waste” investment project by fraudsters claiming to work for electricity companies, police said on Wednesday.

The victim met the first scammer on Facebook and continued conversations on WhatsApp. The fraudster claimed to be a CLP Power employee collaborating with State Grid Corporation of China on an environmental project and directed transfers to multiple personal bank accounts. When the victim raised doubts, the scammer produced a handwritten “guarantee” and a forged Hong Kong identity card photo, then another person posing as a State Grid staff member displayed a fake cheque for HK$9 million to solicit further transfers.

Police said they had received more than 50 investment scam reports in the past week with total losses exceeding HK$30 million. They advised the public to verify identities through official channels and not to transfer money on the basis of claims of high returns or internal staff status.

zh.headline: 男子誤信「環保廢料計劃」失逾280萬 一周逾50宗投資騙案
zh.dek: 騙徒冒充中電及國家電網職員，過去一周投資騙案總損失逾3000萬元。
body: 警方星期三表示，一名約60歲男子誤信「環保廢料計劃」投資騙局，損失超過280萬元。
事主在Facebook認識騙徒後轉用WhatsApp聯絡。對方自稱中電職員，訛稱與國家電網合作環保廢料項目，指示事主將款項轉入多個個人銀行戶口。事主提出質疑時，騙徒展示手寫「保證書」及偽造香港身份證照片，其後另一名自稱國家電網職員的騙徒展示聲稱價值900萬元的偽造支票，誘使再轉賬。
警方指過去一周接獲逾50宗投資騙案，總損失超過3000萬元，提醒市民投資前應透過官方渠道核實身份，切勿輕信高回報零風險聲稱。
